problems.title: Reconstruct Itinerary
problems.statement: Reconstruct airline itinerary starting from JFK using all tickets exactly once. Return lexicographically smallest itinerary.
problems.understanding: Eulerian Path problem on directed graph. Hierholzer's Algorithm builds post-order itinerary traversing sorted neighbors.
problems.intuition: Hierholzer's algorithm: sort destination lists reverse-alphabetically, pop destinations during DFS, append node post-order, then reverse result.
problems.approach:
1. Sort tickets reverse alphabetically so pop() gives smallest destination.
  2. DFS starting from JFK: while neighbors exist, dfs(neighbors.pop()).
  3. Append airport to result post-order. Return reverse of result.

problems.title: Min Cost to Connect All Points
problems.statement: Return minimum cost to connect all points (Manhattan distance |x1-x2| + |y1-y2|).
problems.understanding: Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) problem on complete graph using Prim's algorithm.

naive.title: Naive Solution
naive.html: Kruskal's algorithm building and sorting all N^2 edges.

problems.intuition: Prim's algorithm with min-heap dynamically tracks minimum edge cost from current MST tree to unvisited nodes.
problems.approach:
1. Min-heap [(0, 0)], visited set, total_cost = 0.
  2. Pop (cost, node). If visited continue. Add to visited, add cost.
  3. For all unvisited points: compute distance, push to min-heap.

problems.title: Network Delay Time
problems.statement: Return minimum time for all n nodes to receive signal from source node k. Return -1 if impossible.
problems.understanding: Single-source shortest path on weighted directed graph with non-negative edge weights → Dijkstra's Algorithm!
problems.intuition: Dijkstra's with Min-Heap pops minimum distance node greedily. Maximum distance in final visited map is total time.
problems.approach:
1. Build graph adjacency list (neighbor, weight).
  2. Min-heap [(0, k)], distances map = {}.
  3. Pop (time, node). If node visited continue. Save distances[node] = time.
  4. Push unvisited neighbors with time + weight.
  5. Return max(distances.values()) if len(distances) == n else -1.

problems.title: Swim in Rising Water
problems.statement: Return minimum time t to reach bottom-right (n-1, n-1) from (0,0) in grid of water elevations.
problems.understanding: Shortest path where path cost is max(elevation along path). Solved via Modified Dijkstra.

naive.title: Naive Solution
naive.html: Binary search on time t with BFS check.

problems.intuition: Dijkstra's Algorithm with Min-Heap pops grid cells ordered by max_elevation along path.
problems.approach:
1. Min-heap [(grid[0][0], 0, 0)], visited = {(0,0)}.
  2. Pop (time, r, c). If (r, c) == (n-1, n-1), return time.
  3. Push unvisited neighbors with max(time, grid[nr][nc]).

problems.title: Alien Dictionary
problems.statement: Given sorted dictionary of alien language words, return valid ordering of letters in alien alphabet. If invalid return "".
problems.understanding: Topological Sort on DAG formed by directed edges comparing adjacent words in dictionary.
problems.intuition: Compare adjacent words to extract directed character edges. Post-order DFS topological sort with cycle detection.
problems.approach:
1. Compare adjacent words w1, w2. If w1 starts with w2 and len(w1) > len(w2) return "".
  2. Find first differing char and add edge w1[j] -> w2[j].
  3. Post-order DFS with cycle detection. Return reversed post-order list.

problems.title: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
problems.statement: Return cheapest price from src to dst with at most k stops. If no path, return -1.
problems.understanding: Shortest path with step limit constraint (at most K+1 edges). Ideal for Bellman-Ford algorithm!

naive.title: Naive Solution
naive.html: Dijkstra-style search over (cost, city, flights taken) that respects the k-stop limit but keeps no visited set, so the same city can be expanded many times — correct, but it may explore every route of up to k + 1 flights.
complexity: Time: O(d^(k+1) · log) — d = max flights out of a city

problems.intuition: Bellman-Ford algorithm run K+1 iterations using a copy of previous distances array.
problems.approach:
1. Distance array prices = [inf] * n, prices[src] = 0.
  2. Loop k + 1 times: copy tmp = list(prices). For u, v, w in flights: if prices[u] != inf, update tmp[v] = min(tmp[v], prices[u] + w).
  3. Set prices = tmp. Return prices[dst] if prices[dst] != inf else -1.
